systems_law.name: origin-before-equivalence
systems_law.statement: A shared surface token is not a proof obligation. Resolve source origin, namespace/receiver identity, and short-name collisions before semantic qualification. Only surviving project-local distinctions should consume prover effort.
systems_law.consequence: On the pinned three-corpus FLT scout, the apparent 73-equivalence UNKNOWN residual contains zero surviving project-to-project bridge obligations after origin resolution.

warranted: exact-name presence was checked in all three pinned Mathlib environments
short declaration multiplicity was checked in all three pinned Mathlib source trees
project-local definitions were scanned on exact pinned corpus sources
candidate routing/collision rejection is deterministic under these pins
not_warranted: SAME_UPSTREAM alone does not prove cross-version definitional equality
collision rejection does not prove the colliding objects are semantically unrelated
arbitrary proof-object transport across Lean versions
completeness outside the scanned three-corpus boundary

negative_lineage.finding: first Lean environment probe macro interpolated an identifier expression incorrectly
source declaration regex was over-escaped, yielding zero short-name declarations and exposing the need to test the probe itself

negative_lineage.correction: fixed source regex; all three environments report 71/76 short declaration names present and 12 multiply-declared short names before candidate-specific refinement

revocation_boundary: any pinned corpus or Mathlib source changes
declaration extraction or namespace rules change
